claim: LLM help does not improve human problem-frame quality (280 participants, three LLM modes), widens the experienced/novice gap and lowers novice agency.
note: Three agents fetched the same CHI 2025 paper. One study, but large and controlled. It tests humans using LLMs, not an LLM framing alone.

claim: LLM design agents and generative AI fixate on familiar solutions (repetition, lower novelty).
note: Xu 2026 (preprint, 1 problem), Chen 2025 (preprint, 10 designers), Wadinambiarachchi 2024 (snippet only, human users of image AI), Ege 2024 hackathon (preprint). Weak individually; direction agrees. Wadinambiarachchi is adjacent: human fixation induced by AI images.

claim: External co-regulation of an LLM design agent beats self-regulation, which beats a plain loop, at similar compute.
note: One preprint, one battery-pack problem. Do not transfer to puzzles.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without external feedback often fails or hurts; it works with reliable external feedback.
note: Huang 2023 and Kamoi 2024 survey. Strong support for reframing on real check output, not on a timer.

claim: More deliberation, longer reasoning or chain of thought can lower accuracy on some tasks.
note: Liu 2024 (preprint), Gema 2025, Chen 2024 (preprint). Matches our puzzle losses. Task families are not design tasks.

claim: AI idea access raises individual creativity but reduces diversity across people; samples from one model are alike.
note: Doshi 2023 plus Chen 2025 and Bruggeman 2025 (clustering of GPT-4o outputs). Supports forced divergence for open tasks.

claim: Human design fixation from examples is real (Jansson and Smith), but effect sizes vary widely by setup and no pooled estimate exists.
note: Vasconcelos and Crilly fetched (25 studies, wide variance). Jansson and Smith and Sio et al. rest on memory or snippet. The phenomenon is established; the size is not.

claim: Analogy-style methods raise novelty, but novelty gain and fixation reduction are separate (WordTree reduced fixation, SCAMPER did not).
note: One 97-expert experiment fetched. The review supports only that results vary. Measure both outcomes.

claim: Problem and solution co-evolve; creative moments come from a bridge between a refined frame and a partial solution.
note: Nine designers, one task, all lines from memory. A critique exists (Kokotovich) but is unread. No LLM test at equal tokens (design-a-15).

claim: No single design strategy (problem-driven, solution-driven, etc.) predicts better solutions.
note: Kruger and Cross, nine designers, memory only, never fetched.

claim: Experts scope the problem longer and gather more information than novices; reflective attention to back talk rises with seniority.
note: Three papers, all memory-only, from one research cluster (Atman, Adams, Cross) with shared frameworks. Counted as one line. Seniority is confounded with other skills.

claim: Primary generator: designers adopt an early simple idea and test it.
Reflection-in-action has no controlled test as a procedure.
note: Absence claim from memory; the search was thin.

claim: Less experienced users adopt AI output directly; experienced designers assess it critically.
note: Chen 2025 (preprint, 10 people) and Shin 2025 agree in direction. Both are about human users, not agents.

claim: GPT-4o scores below human designer groups on latent-need elicitation and mostly restates surface attributes.
note: One exploratory study, 5 designers per group. Authors call it small.

claim: An LLM agent abandoned promising ideas after minor difficulties in a hackathon, despite strong concept generation.
note: Preprint, one team. Anecdotal, but hints at a persistence step.

claim: Prompting LLMs with problem-driven or solution-driven styles gives human-like features and more novel outputs but not nonlinear problem-solution switching; curated reasoning tools help human designers.
note: Zhang 2025 reports gains, but the Wang study is a human interface study, not an agent procedure, and the ICCC paper was unreadable. Low credibility.

claim: LLM critics and assistants tend toward sycophancy, which can weaken a reflection or critic call that reads the draft.
note: Sharma 2023 preprint. Not tested on self-critique in design. Argues for blind or separate-context critics.

claim: No controlled test shows a Dorst-Cross procedure inside an LLM beats plain generation at equal tokens.
note: Absence claim; the search budget ran out. Not established as absence.
